messages:
Sofia M.: Heads up — ACH return on invoice #5301 (Aurelia Systems) for $32,412.30, return code R07 (authorization revoked). BillingBot posted the event earlier.
BillingBot: Automated: payment_failed - invoice:5301 - amount:$32412.30 - method:ACH - return_code:R07 - ts:2026-03-05T08:12:09Z
Dmitri P.: Oof. do we have the ACH agreement scanned? and any procurement contact?
Sofia M.: Yes, scanned copy is on the billing portal (AUTH-2024-112). AE listed procurement@aureliasys.com as billing contact. left voicemail + sent our standard dunning email an hour ago.
Laila H.: For dollars this size, we shouldn't immediately send to external collections. propose: (A) one re-present attempt, (B) offer a short 2-installment plan (50/50 in 14 days each) if they confirm in writing within 5 business days, (C) waive late fee if they accept the plan.
Dmitri P.: I prefer re-present once, but if they claim revocation we need to stop and involve Legal. Also ask Sales to try procurement contact before we reattempt.
Sofia M.: Agreed. Plan I propose: 1) Schedule ACH re-present at next bank window (2026-03-06 09:00 PT). 2) Send escalation email CC'ing AE and SalesOps with proposed 50/50 plan and fee waiver (waive $250 if signed within 5 days). 3) Hold escalation to external collections for 10 days to allow plan acceptance. 4) If they dispute auth, stop attempts and route to Legal Ops.
CollectionsBot: Policy note: R07 with signed auth allows one re-present. If re-present fails and customer disputes, hold further attempts and escalate to Legal Ops. Default collections escalation after 10 days if no arrangement.
Dmitri P.: please include a clear dispute path and require supporting docs. Legal Ops, can you review the plan text quickly?
Legal Ops: Reviewing. Key point: mention that re-present is one-time and reference auth id. Also add sentence about dispute escalation to reduce chargeback exposure.
Sofia M.: Draft email below — feedback welcome:

"Hi Aurelia Systems — We attempted ACH collection for invoice #5301 ($32,412.30) on 2026-03-05 but it was returned (R07: authorization revoked). We have an executed ACH authorization on file (AUTH-2024-112). As a one-time courtesy we will reattempt the ACH on 2026-03-06. If that attempt fails, we would like to offer a short payment arrangement: two equal installments, due 14 and 28 days from acceptance. If you confirm acceptance in writing within 5 business days, Redwood will waive the $250 late fee. If you dispute the ACH authorization, please reply within 5 business days with supporting documentation and we will pause collection activity and involve Legal Ops. If we do not receive a response or payment/arrangement within 10 days, this invoice will be routed to collections.

Regards,
Redwood Billing Team"

Laila H.: Language looks good. add line: "Payments accepted via card or wire if you prefer; card payments will incur a 2.5% processing fee."
Sofia M.: added. scheduling re-present now and tagging SalesOps to ping procurement.
BillingBot: Action logged: reattempt_scheduled - invoice:5301 - attempt_time:2026-03-06T16:00:00Z - initiated_by:Sofia M.
Dmitri P.: Also add CRM note: dunning_status = reattempt_pending; flagged for AE follow-up.
Sofia M.: CRM updated. AE (Liam) pinged procurement.
Laila H.: If they accept the installment plan, require e-sign on the arrangement doc and autopay setup for the second installment. we can't rely on a verbal agreement.
Legal Ops: Agreed. add requirement: signed arrangement + autopay for installments; otherwise escalate.
Sofia M.: Confirmed with Legal Ops. I'll send the email with legal in CC and schedule the bank re-present.
CollectionsBot: Reminder scheduled: escalate invoice 5301 to collections queue after 10 days (2026-03-16) if status != PAID or ARRANGED.
Sofia M.: Call with AE complete — procurement is checking with their finance team and said they'd get back within 48 hours. leaving thread open and will update after re-present. :phone:
